additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food within a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control over eating, occurring at least weekly for three months. Episodes are typically followed by marked distress such as shame, guilt, or disgust, but unlike bulimia nervosa, there are no regular compensatory behaviors like vomiting, fasting, or excessive exercise. The disorder often emerges in the context of dieting, weight concerns, mood or anxiety disorders, or chronic stress, and can fluctuate in severity over time. It is associated with functional impairment, medical comorbidities (e.g., obesity, metabolic syndrome), and psychosocial difficulties, and is distinguished from occasional overeating by its frequency, loss of control, and emotional impact.

patient.stressor: In the past year, Maria’s husband developed worsening mobility and heart problems, and she quietly became his primary caregiver, managing medications, appointments, and most household tasks. This new responsibility layered on top of her own aging-related fatigue, leading her to cut back on community center volunteering and choir, which had been important outlets for connection and routine. During a stressful three-month stretch when her husband had two brief hospitalizations, she found herself staying home more, cooking large batches of her traditional dishes "just in case" and then picking at them alone late into the night after he was asleep, using food as a familiar comfort in the face of worry and isolation. She agreed to see a mental health provider at the suggestion of her primary care doctor after admitting she felt increasingly ashamed about how she was eating in private and that the guilt afterward was making it harder to enjoy the family meals and church gatherings she usually treasured.
patient.chief_complaint: After some of these big eating spells, I just feel disgusted with myself and very guilty about what I’ve done.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: Lately I’ll make a big pot of rice and stew or a whole tray of baked chicken “so there’s enough,” and then sit at the kitchen table and just keep going back for seconds and thirds until I’ve eaten what my whole family would normally finish in one Sunday dinner, all by myself, in an evening.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like something takes over my hands—I'll be telling myself, 'Maria, stop, you don’t need more,' but I keep scooping food onto my plate and eating it anyway, like I can’t hit the brakes.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat so fast during these times that I hardly chew or taste anything, just shoveling it in as if I’m racing, and only afterward do I realize the plate is empty and I barely remember eating it.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: I keep eating past the point where my belly feels tight and heavy, to where it hurts to bend over and I have to sit very still in my chair because I’m so stuffed it makes me a little sick.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: After one of those nights, when the dishes are piled in the sink and my husband is asleep in the next room, I just sit there staring at the empty pots, calling myself a pig and feeling so ashamed and guilty that I’ve done it again instead of being stronger for him and for myself.
